evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/main.rs:453 — production wiring constructs the saved-search alert delivery worker as `SearchAlertDrainerWorker::new(...)`, which (services/search_alert_drainer.rs:187-194) hard-codes the logging stub transports `Arc::new(LogEmailTransport)` / `Arc::new(LogPushTransport)`. The real SMTP/FCM/APNs adapters are only injectable via the alternate `with_transports(...)` constructor, which main.rs never calls.

services/search_alert_drainer.rs:136 (default config, line 133-138) sets `enabled: true`, so the drainer runs by default in production; `LogEmailTransport::send_email` unconditionally returns `Ok(())`. In `run_once` (services/search_alert_drainer.rs:280-329) a successful email send sets `any_ok = true`, and at line 316-322 `any_ok` triggers `self.repo.mark_search_alert_notified(alert.id)` which stamps the `notified_at` column (migration 00195).

Net effect: in production every `search_alert_queue` row is marked notified after being merely written to the log — no email/push is actually delivered, yet the row is permanently recorded as delivered. Because `list_undelivered_search_alerts` filters on `notified_at`, when a real transport is later injected via `with_transports` those already-stamped alerts will be skipped forever and never re-sent. Silent out-of-band notification loss plus a one-way cutover data-loss hazard (the in-app feed channel, keyed on `status`, is unaffected, which masks the problem).

Fix (concrete, cloud-landable): gate the mark-notified so a stub/log transport does not count as a real delivery (e.g. add an `is_real_delivery()` on the transport trait, or have `LogEmailTransport` return `Err`/a `Skipped` outcome so `any_ok` stays false), OR default `SearchAlertDrainerConfig::enabled` to `false` until a real transport is wired into main.rs. Either prevents rows from being irrevocably marked delivered while only the logging stubs are mounted.
